newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's Reform abandons official opposition bid.
newsitem.headline: Canada's Reform abandons official opposition bid.

text.p: Canada's Reform Party abandoned on Wednesday its latest bid to oust the separatist Bloc Quebecois as official opposition in the House of Commons, after failing to win the support of independent members.
Reform is tied with the Bloc at 50 members of Parliament each and argues it is more suited as a government-in-waiting than a party dedicated to breaking up Canada.
Last month, Reform leader Preston Manning challenged the 16 members who do not belong to the ruling Liberals, the Bloc or Reform to support Reform's bid to replace the Bloc.
But he said today that none agreed.
"Each of them chose to put their partisan reasons ahead of federalism versus separatism and this is something we'd like to hold them accountable for in their ridings," Manning told reporters.
"Canadians will ultimately decide this issue at the polls."
A federal election is widely expected in June or October.
